fullText.simplified:
第十六章、我又被流放了

    在楚怀王被秦王抓住的第三年，楚国接到了最坏的消息——楚怀王在秦国病死了。
    秦国把死了的楚怀王送回楚国。楚国的每条街道上都能听到楚国百姓的哭声。我的声音早就哭坏了，现在哭不出来，也骂不出来了。
    我站在街上，看着灰色的天，听着百姓们伤心的哭声，心里难过极了。
    “我的理想也一直都在。”这是楚怀王最后对我说的话。他说的是真的，他到死都没有同意秦王的要求，到死都在坚持自己的理想。
    楚国的橘子，楚怀王吃不到了，但他变成了一棵橘树。
    不久后，我收到通知，新王要我去楚国的南方流放。
    又要离开引都了。从二十岁来到引都，我在这儿已经生活了二十多年。现在离开，不知道以后还能不能回来。我站在城门口，最后看了一眼引都和城里的百姓。
    我不害怕流放，但新王和子兰拿走了我为楚国工作的机会。他们把我变成一个空有理想，但无法为理想而工作的人，这是最让我痛苦的。
    楚国的南方和北方不一样，南方的山更高，水更深。我有时候坐船，有时候走路。从春到夏，从夏到冬，一年又一年。
    有时候，我穿着破旧的单衣，和辛苦的百姓们坐在一起吃简单的饭菜。这时候我会忘了引都，忘了楚怀王。但吃完饭，一个人走在河边，看着天上向北飞去的鸟儿，我又会感到难过。
    天黑了，鸟儿飞累了，它会回家。有些动物，一生过完了，快死的时候，它会看向出生的方向，那儿有它的家。我一直望着北方，那儿有引都。
    我知道，只要我不把理想放下，痛苦就会一直跟着我。但是我就是放不下，我放不下一天天走向危险的楚国，放不下辛苦一生却看不到希望的楚国百姓。
fullText.traditional:
第十六章、我又被流放了

    在楚懷王被秦王抓住的第三年，楚國接到了最壞的消息——楚懷王在秦國病死了。
    秦國把死了的楚懷王送回楚國。楚國的每條街道上都能聽到楚國百姓的哭聲。我的聲音早就哭壞了，現在哭不出來，也罵不出來了。
    我站在街上，看著灰色的天，聽著百姓們傷心的哭聲，心裡難過極了。
    “我的理想也一直都在。”這是楚懷王最後對我說的話。他說的是真的，他到死都沒有同意秦王的要求，到死都在堅持自己的理想。
    楚國的橘子，楚懷王吃不到了，但他變成了一棵橘樹。
    不久後，我收到通知，新王要我去楚國的南方流放。
    又要離開引都了。從二十歲來到引都，我在這兒已經生活了二十多年。現在離開，不知道以後還能不能回來。我站在城門口，最後看了一眼引都和城裡的百姓。
    我不害怕流放，但新王和子蘭拿走了我為楚國工作的機會。他們把我變成一個空有理想，但無法為理想而工作的人，這是最讓我痛苦的。
    楚國的南方和北方不一樣，南方的山更高，水更深。我有時候坐船，有時候走路。從春到夏，從夏到冬，一年又一年。
    有時候，我穿著破舊的單衣，和辛苦的百姓們坐在一起吃簡單的飯菜。這時候我會忘了引都，忘了楚懷王。但吃完飯，一個人走在河邊，看著天上向北飛去的鳥兒，我又會感到難過。
    天黑了，鳥兒飛累了，牠會回家。有些動物，一生過完了，快死的時候，牠會看向出生的方向，那兒有牠的家。我一直望著北方，那兒有引都。
    我知道，只要我不把理想放下，痛苦就會一直跟著我。但是我就是放不下，我放不下一天天走向危險的楚國，放不下辛苦一生卻看不到希望的楚國百姓。

sentences.simplified: 在楚怀王被秦王抓住的第三年，楚国接到了最坏的消息——楚怀王在秦国病死了。
sentences.traditional: 在楚懷王被秦王抓住的第三年，楚國接到了最壞的消息——楚懷王在秦國病死了。
sentences.pinyin: zài chǔ huái wáng bèi qín wáng zhuā zhù de dì sān nián chǔ guó jiē dào le zuì huài de xiāo xi chǔ huái wáng zài qín guó bìng sǐ le
sentences.english: In the third year after King Huai of Chu was captured by the King of Qin, Chu received the worst news—King Huai had died of illness in Qin.

sentences.simplified: 秦国把死了的楚怀王送回楚国。楚国的每条街道上都能听到楚国百姓的哭声。
sentences.traditional: 秦國把死了的楚懷王送回楚國。楚國的每條街道上都能聽到楚國百姓的哭聲。
sentences.pinyin: qín guó bǎ sǐ le de chǔ huái wáng sòng huí chǔ guó chǔ guó de měi tiáo jiē dào shang dōu néng tīng dào chǔ guó bǎi xìng de kū shēng
sentences.english: Qin sent the remains of King Huai of Chu back to Chu. The sobs of the people of Chu could be heard on every street.

sentences.simplified: 我的声音早就哭坏了，现在哭不出来，也骂不出来了。
sentences.traditional: 我的聲音早就哭壞了，現在哭不出來，也罵不出來了。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ de shēng yīn zǎo jiù kū huài le xiàn zài kū bù chu lai yě mà bù chu lai le
sentences.english: My voice had long gone hoarse from crying, and now I couldn’t cry or curse anymore.

sentences.simplified: 我站在街上，看着灰色的天，听着百姓们伤心的哭声，心里难过极了。
sentences.traditional: 我站在街上，看著灰色的天，聽著百姓們傷心的哭聲，心裡難過極了。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ zhàn zài jiē shang kàn zhe huī sè de tiān tīng zhe bǎi xìng men shāng xīn de kū shēng xīn lǐ nán guò jí le
sentences.english: I stood on the street, looking at the gray sky and listening to the sorrowful cries of the people, feeling extremely sad inside.

sentences.simplified: “我的理想也一直都在。”这是楚怀王最后对我说的话。
sentences.traditional: “我的理想也一直都在。”這是楚懷王最後對我說的話。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ de lǐ xiǎng yě yì zhí dōu zài zhè shì chǔ huái wáng zuì hòu duì wǒ shuō de huà
sentences.english: “My ideals have always endured.” That was the last thing King Huai of Chu said to me.

sentences.simplified: 他说的是真的，他到死都没有同意秦王的要求，到死都在坚持自己的理想。
sentences.traditional: 他說的是真的，他到死都沒有同意秦王的要求，到死都在堅持自己的理想。
sentences.pinyin: tā shuō de shì zhēn de tā dào sǐ dōu méi yǒu tóng yì qín wáng de yāo qiú dào sǐ dōu zài jiān chí zì jǐ de lǐ xiǎng
sentences.english: He was telling the truth. To his dying day, he never agreed to the King of Qin’s demands; to his dying day, he held to his ideals.

sentences.simplified: 楚国的橘子，楚怀王吃不到了，但他变成了一棵橘树。
sentences.traditional: 楚國的橘子，楚懷王吃不到了，但他變成了一棵橘樹。
sentences.pinyin: chǔ guó de jú zi chǔ huái wáng chī bú dào le dàn tā biàn chéng le yì kē jú shù
sentences.english: King Huai of Chu could no longer eat the oranges of Chu, but he had become an orange tree.

sentences.simplified: 不久后，我收到通知，新王要我去楚国的南方流放。
sentences.traditional: 不久後，我收到通知，新王要我去楚國的南方流放。
sentences.pinyin: bù jiǔ hòu wǒ shōu dào tōng zhī xīn wáng yào wǒ qù chǔ guó de nán fāng liú fàng
sentences.english: Not long after, I received a notice that the new king wanted to banish me to the south of Chu.

sentences.simplified: 又要离开引都了。从二十岁来到引都，我在这儿已经生活了二十多年。
sentences.traditional: 又要離開引都了。從二十歲來到引都，我在這兒已經生活了二十多年。
sentences.pinyin: yòu yào lí kāi yǐn dū le cóng èr shí suì lái dào yǐn dū wǒ zài zhè‘r yǐ jīng shēng huó le èr shí duō nián
sentences.english: I had to leave Yindu again. Since coming to Yindu at the age of twenty, I had lived here for more than twenty years.

sentences.simplified: 现在离开，不知道以后还能不能回来。
sentences.traditional: 現在離開，不知道以後還能不能回來。
sentences.pinyin: xiàn zài lí kāi bù zhī dào yǐ hòu hái néng bù néng huí lái
sentences.english: Now that I was leaving, I didn’t know if I would be able to return in the future.

sentences.simplified: 我站在城门口，最后看了一眼引都和城里的百姓。
sentences.traditional: 我站在城門口，最後看了一眼引都和城裡的百姓。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ zhàn zài chéng mén kǒu zuì hòu kàn le yì yǎn yǐn dū hé chéng lǐ de bǎi xìng
sentences.english: I stood at the city gate, taking one last look at Yindu and the people in the city.

sentences.simplified: 我不害怕流放，但新王和子兰拿走了我为楚国工作的机会。
sentences.traditional: 我不害怕流放，但新王和子蘭拿走了我為楚國工作的機會。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ bú hài pà liú fàng dàn xīn wáng hé zǐ lán ná zǒu le wǒ wèi chǔ guó gōng zuò de jī huì
sentences.english: I was not afraid of exile, but the new king and Zilan had taken away my opportunity to work for Chu.

sentences.simplified: 他们把我变成一个空有理想，但无法为理想而工作的人，这是最让我痛苦的。
sentences.traditional: 他們把我變成一個空有理想，但無法為理想而工作的人，這是最讓我痛苦的。
sentences.pinyin: tā men bǎ wǒ biàn chéng yí ge kōng yǒu lǐ xiǎng dàn wú fǎ wèi lǐ xiǎng ér gōng zuò de rén zhè shì zuì ràng wǒ tòng kǔ de
sentences.english: They turned me into someone whose ideals were held in vain, unable to work for them. This is what pained me the most.

sentences.simplified: 楚国的南方和北方不一样，南方的山更高，水更深。
sentences.traditional: 楚國的南方和北方不一樣，南方的山更高，水更深。
sentences.pinyin: chǔ guó de nán fāng hé běi fāng bù yí yàng nán fāng de shān gèng gāo shuǐ gèng shēn
sentences.english: The south of the state of Chu was different from the north; the mountains in the south were higher, and the rivers were deeper.

sentences.simplified: 我有时候坐船，有时候走路。从春到夏，从夏到冬，一年又一年。
sentences.traditional: 我有時候坐船，有時候走路。從春到夏，從夏到冬，一年又一年。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ yǒu shí hou zuò chuán yǒu shí hou zǒu lù cóng chūn dào xià cóng xià dào dōng yì nián yòu yì nián
sentences.english: Sometimes I traveled by boat, sometimes on foot. From spring to summer, from summer to winter, one year followed another.

sentences.simplified: 有时候，我穿着破旧的单衣，和辛苦的百姓们坐在一起吃简单的饭菜。
sentences.traditional: 有時候，我穿著破舊的單衣，和辛苦的百姓們坐在一起吃簡單的飯菜。
sentences.pinyin: yǒu shí hou wǒ chuān zhe pò jiù de dān yī hé xīn kǔ de bǎi xìng men zuò zài yì qǐ chī jiǎn dān de fàn cài
sentences.english: Sometimes, I wore worn-out clothes and sat with the hardworking common people, eating simple meals.

sentences.simplified: 这时候我会忘了引都，忘了楚怀王。
sentences.traditional: 這時候我會忘了引都，忘了楚懷王。
sentences.pinyin: zhè shí hou wǒ huì wàng le yǐn dū wàng le chǔ huái wáng
sentences.english: At these times, I would forget about Yindu and King Huai of Chu.

sentences.simplified: 但吃完饭，一个人走在河边，看着天上向北飞去的鸟儿，我又会感到难过。
sentences.traditional: 但吃完飯，一個人走在河邊，看著天上向北飛去的鳥兒，我又會感到難過。
sentences.pinyin: dàn chī wán fàn yí ge rén zǒu zài hé biān kàn zhe tiān shàng xiàng běi fēi qù de niǎo'r wǒ yòu huì gǎn dào nán guò
sentences.english: But after the meals, as I walked alone by the river and watched the birds in the sky flying north, I would feel sad again.

sentences.simplified: 天黑了，鸟儿飞累了，它会回家。
sentences.traditional: 天黑了，鳥兒飛累了，牠會回家。
sentences.pinyin: tiān hēi le niǎo'r fēi lèi le tā huì huí jiā
sentences.english: When night falls and the birds grow tired of flying, they return home.

sentences.simplified: 有些动物，一生过完了，快死的时候，
sentences.traditional: 有些動物，一生過完了，快死的時候，
sentences.pinyin: yǒu xiē dòng wù yì shēng guò wán le kuài sǐ de shí hou
sentences.english: Some animals, when their lives are coming to an end and they are about to die, ..

sentences.simplified: 它会看向出生的方向，那儿有它的家。
sentences.traditional: 牠會看向出生的方向，那兒有牠的家。
sentences.pinyin: tā huì kàn xiàng chū shēng de fāng xiàng nà'r yǒu tā de jiā
sentences.english: .. will look toward the direction where they were born, where their home is.

sentences.simplified: 我一直望着北方，那儿有引都。
sentences.traditional: 我一直望著北方，那兒有引都。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ yì zhí wàng zhe běi fāng nà'r yǒu yǐn dū
sentences.english: I always gazed north, where Yindu was.

sentences.simplified: 我知道，只要我不把理想放下，痛苦就会一直跟着我。
sentences.traditional: 我知道，只要我不把理想放下，痛苦就會一直跟著我。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ zhī dào zhǐ yào wǒ bù bǎ lǐ xiǎng fàng xià tòng kǔ jiù huì yì zhí gēn zhe wǒ
sentences.english: I knew that as long as I didn’t give up my ideals, pain would always follow me.

sentences.simplified: 但是我就是放不下，
sentences.traditional: 但是我就是放不下，
sentences.pinyin: dàn shì wǒ jiù shì fàng bú xià
sentences.english: But I just couldn’t let go.

sentences.simplified: 我放不下一天天走向危险的楚国，
sentences.traditional: 我放不下一天天走向危險的楚國，
sentences.pinyin: wǒ fàng bú xià yì tiān tiān zǒu xiàng wēi xiǎn de chǔ guó
sentences.english: I couldn’t let go of the state of Chu, which was heading into danger day by day, ..

sentences.simplified: 放不下辛苦一生却看不到希望的楚国百姓。
sentences.traditional: 放不下辛苦一生卻看不到希望的楚國百姓。
sentences.pinyin: fàng bú xià xīn kǔ yì shēng què kàn bú dào xī wàng de chǔ guó bǎi xìng
sentences.english: .. nor could I let go of the people of Chu who toiled all their lives yet saw no hope.

sentence_translations: Chapter 16: I Am Banished Again
In the third year after King Huai of Chu was captured by the King of Qin, Chu received the worst news—King Huai had died of illness in Qin.
Qin sent the remains of King Huai of Chu back to Chu. The sobs of the people of Chu could be heard on every street.
My voice had long gone hoarse from crying, and now I couldn’t cry or curse anymore.
I stood on the street, looking at the gray sky and listening to the sorrowful cries of the people, feeling extremely sad inside.
“My ideals have always endured.” That was the last thing King Huai of Chu said to me.
He was telling the truth. To his dying day, he never agreed to the King of Qin’s demands; to his dying day, he held to his ideals.
King Huai of Chu could no longer eat the oranges of Chu, but he had become an orange tree.
Not long after, I received a notice that the new king wanted to banish me to the south of Chu.
I had to leave Yindu again. Since coming to Yindu at the age of twenty, I had lived here for more than twenty years.
Now that I was leaving, I didn’t know if I would be able to return in the future.
I stood at the city gate, taking one last look at Yindu and the people in the city.
I was not afraid of exile, but the new king and Zilan had taken away my opportunity to work for Chu.
They turned me into someone whose ideals were held in vain, unable to work for them. This is what pained me the most.
The south of the state of Chu was different from the north; the mountains in the south were higher, and the rivers were deeper.
Sometimes I traveled by boat, sometimes on foot. From spring to summer, from summer to winter, one year followed another.
Sometimes, I wore worn-out clothes and sat with the hardworking common people, eating simple meals.
At these times, I would forget about Yindu and King Huai of Chu.
But after the meals, as I walked alone by the river and watched the birds in the sky flying north, I would feel sad again.
When night falls and the birds grow tired of flying, they return home.
Some animals, when their lives are coming to an end and they are about to die, ..
.. will look toward the direction where they were born, where their home is.
I always gazed north, where Yindu was.
I knew that as long as I didn’t give up my ideals, pain would always follow me.
But I just couldn’t let go.
I couldn’t let go of the state of Chu, which was heading into danger day by day, ..
.. nor could I let go of the people of Chu who toiled all their lives yet saw no hope.
